posts.preview: Trade unions are strategic partners to government and employers. Many trade unions invest heavily in capacity building for their representatives so they can effectively represent and protect their members

Part of this training includes helping employers understand and comply with labour legislation. This contributes to healthier workplaces, stronger industrial relations, and business growth because employees become more confident, informed, and secure in their workplaces

The constant negative labels used to describe trade unions—such as “troublemakers,” “useless,” or “thieves”—can create division between workers and the very institutions established to protect their interests. Such division and hostility ultimately benefit those who would rather see workers without a collective voice

My urgent call is that every worker in Namibia should consider reaching out to a recognised trade union and joining one as an investment in their protection and representation.
